finding.text: `Servex/leaks.mjs` `pair()` (diff lines 831-839) runs `starts.find` for every line and `starts.find` + `ends.find` for every start, so it is O(n²). The doc measures about 38 sampled starts and 42 ends a minute, which is about 55k starts a day, so within a day or two the report takes minutes to run. Index starts and ends by pid in a Map first.

A Servex restart drops both `Lineage.known` and SpawnLog's `child.once("exit")` listeners. Any process that dies during the restart gap, and any SpawnLog-started process that outlives the restart (an adopted dev server whose parent is the old Servex, so Lineage finds no ancestor), never gets an end line. Each one will show up as "gone, end missed" forever. Either reload the open starts at boot (for example from `leaks.mjs`'s `pair()`) and end them on the first sample, or name this limit in `Servex/doc/processes.md` "Sampled children" next to the 10 s limit. Right now the doc lists no restart limit.

`Servex/doc/processes.md` (diff line 782) says that for a detached grandchild with no line, "the leak report below still shows it in the process list". `leaks.mjs` reads only log lines (`read_lines`); it never lists unlogged processes, so that claim is false. Drop the clause or point it at `Lifecycle.js --dry`.

The test's junk start line for pid 101 (`ai/sessions/2026/09/30/2976c23c-…/process-monitor/task.jsonl`, started 1969) will be the "gone" row in every future report. Appending a matching `{"pid_exit":101,"ended":<now>,"code":null,"seen":"sample"}` would close it without rewriting history.

Volume: about 80 lines a minute across 7 agents go into git-tracked `session.jsonl` files, which is about 115k lines a day. The 60/min cap is per agent, so it does not bound the total. Owner's call; worth a line in processes.md.

`Lifecycle.kill()` (diff line 144) fails open: `owners_own(this.procs?.get(pid))` is false when `procs` is unset or lacks the pid, so the guard only works when the table is loaded. `!this.procs?.has(pid) || owners_own(...)` would refuse instead. (A missing pid is most likely already dead.)

`OUR_CHROME`'s `[\\/]lew42[\\/]` arm (Lifecycle.js, diff line 125) matches no profile any code launches; only the test's made-up `lew42\chrome-profile` uses it. Because `resources()` now uses `OUR_CHROME`, this arm widens what the sweep may reap after 30 min. The shared headed Chrome at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\claude-shared-chrome` is not matched, which is correct. Drop the arm unless a real profile lives there.

`Server/Browser.mjs:18`: the exit hook can write a second end line when the async "browser closed" post reached Servex but its `.then` had not run before exit. This is harmless to `open()`, and only cosmetic.
`Servex/Processes.js:449`: the `watch_spin` line picked up an extra tab of indentation.

Outside the fence: `Server/browser-watchdog.mjs`, `Server/doc/browser.md`, `Server/doc/scripts.md` and `Servex/doc/lifecycle.md` were changed. Each is a Browser/Lifecycle close path or its doc, and the change is stated in the task's caveats. Justified.

`node Servex/leaks.mjs` is documented in processes.md and indexing-past-work.md §5. Neither the Servex readme's command block nor `Server/doc/scripts.md` lists it (or `Lineage.js` and the two new tests); one line in the readme's "Where the code is" would index them.
